doc.title: Gap Mangione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012

chapter: Family, solo piano and performing wisdom
title: Family as the source of the music
summary: His family supports his music, including his wife and the ballad Bellezza.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: No. Very well put. Very important. And we’re just about running out of time here. Anything that you want to add that I didn’t really ask about?

Well just what a lot of people don’t see and what exists in a way that’s too hard to explain is family. And I mentioned my kids and my folks, and my wife, who whenever I’m writing a chart hears it the first thousand times that it gets played, right? And then later on at dinner says, “You know I liked the changes you’ve made in that.” But way more than that, the kind of family support, love and all that kind of thing, that’s where the music comes from.

Well, or if you get a chance listen to Gerry Niewood play a song that I love, a song that I wrote for my wife called “Bellezza.” It’s a ballad. It’s a saxophone ballad. And everybody’s got something to say.
